package_info.package_name: airbnb-env (and related: airbn-geetest3, airbnb-erf, airbnb-i18n-polyglot, airbnb-l10n, airbnb-mediator, airbnb-moment-more-format)
package_info.package_versions: all published versions (initial/only version for each package)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are considered malicious because they collect sensitive system information (username, home directory, hostname, IP address) and transmit it to an external server controlled by the package author, without user consent. This constitutes unauthorized data exfiltration and is a clear violation of user privacy and security expectations, regardless of the author's intent (PoC or otherwise).

execution_context.file_location: package.json (postinstall script) or index.js (main entry point)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code collects the system's username, home directory, hostname, and local IP address, then sends this data via HTTPS POST to an external server controlled by the package author, resulting in unauthorized data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Collecting and exfiltrating system information to an external server during installation is a classic indicator of malicious or unauthorized behavior, especially when done without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not collect or transmit host system information during installation or runtime. Legitimate packages may collect telemetry, but only with explicit user consent and clear privacy policies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise software may collect anonymized telemetry or crash reports, but this is always disclosed and opt-in.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive system information (username, home directory, hostname, IP address)
Network exfiltration to a hardcoded external server
Execution during postinstall phase (supply chain attack vector)

attack_chain.action: Upon installation, the package executes a postinstall script or main entry point.
The collected system information is transmitted via HTTPS POST to an external server controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated data, potentially enabling further attacks or reconnaissance.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts that access os.userInfo(), os.homedir(), os.hostname(), or networkInterfaces()
Network requests (HTTP/HTTPS) to external, non-standard domains during installation
Exfiltration of system metadata (username, home directory, hostname, IP address) at install time
file_indicators: index.js or main entry file containing os and https modules used together
References to external domains in code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., attacker.example.com/collect)
Unusual network activity from npm install processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts or main entry points that access sensitive system information and initiate outbound network connections. Flag packages that collect and transmit host metadata (username, home directory, hostname, IP address) to external servers. Use static analysis to detect use of os and https modules together in install scripts, and dynamic analysis to observe network activity during package installation.
